results.title: Helicone Reviews: What Users Really Think - Helicone
results.content:
Cost tracking gaps for new models. Some users report that cost accounting for newly released models can lag provider releases. If your workflow involves rapid adoption of brand-new model SKUs, plan for occasional gaps and validate costs in your provider console during the first days or weeks.

UI and data reliability issues. GitHub includes at least one documented example of dashboard correctness problems, including a request-count bug describing incorrect totals and broken pagination.

Self-hosted coverage questions. Helicone supports self-hosting, and it has documented efforts to make it easier. Still, if you self-host specifically to keep data in your own environment, you should confirm provider coverage and feature parity against your requirements. [...] Last updated

## AI Consensus on Helicone

Proxy-based setup earns strong praise for speed, but depth of agent tracing keeps it off shortlists for complex workflows.

Positive sentiment: +setup simplicityPositive sentiment: +cost & token trackingPositive sentiment: +api gateway cachingNegative sentiment: −agent trace depthMixed sentiment: ±framework integration [...] Changing a single base URL logs every request instantly — "two lines of code" and "under two minutes" appear repeatedly across Reddit threads and comparison guides
 Wins on cost and token tracking across 100+ providers, with built-in caching flagged as a standout money-saver for startups
 Consistently categorized below LangSmith and Langfuse for deep agent debugging; teams needing step-by-step reasoning traces tend to look elsewhere

Based on 30 AI answers

Helicone is an LLM observability platform built to help development teams monitor LLM API calls, track costs across providers, and debug production AI applications. It uses a proxy-based architecture that routes requests through a gateway, which can add observability without deep instrumentation.
